title: Search
subtitle: An inverted index turns an 8-second scan into a few milliseconds, at the cost of a second copy of the data
motto: Index the words, not the rows
keyInsight: Search looks up words instead of scanning rows, and ranks by rarity, but the index is a second copy of your data that trails the database.

decisions.title: Show the stop word as the failure
decisions.description: A word found in 99% of documents makes its posting list as long as the table, so the failure frame shows an index can be nearly as slow as a scan for the wrong word.
decisions.alternatives: Showing only rare-word queries would make the index look fast for every query.

decisions.title: Report the lag with the speed
decisions.description: The last frame carries the refresh interval next to the storage cost, since a fast index is only useful if you accept that it is behind the database.
decisions.alternatives: Leaving out staleness would present the index as free.
